name: MAT
cycle: MAT December 2026 (upcoming session: PBT 20 Dec 2026, CBT 27 Dec 2026)
eligibility: Graduation in any discipline from any recognized University or equivalent recognized degree. A final year student in any undergraduate programme (B.A, B.Sc., B.Com., B.Tech., etc.) can also appear provisionally. No age bar; job experience not necessary. Minimum percentage requirements vary by institute.
mode: Paper Based Test (PBT) and Computer Based Test (CBT); candidates may take one mode or both (PBT+CBT, best score used). Internet Based Test (IBT) is not listed among current official test modes (null).
frequency: Four times a year: February, May, September and December (plus a PBT Special Drive held 6 Sep 2026). A candidate may opt for one or two test modes per session.

pattern.marking: Objective multiple-choice; negative marking of -0.25 marks for every incorrect answer. Marks per correct answer are not stated officially (null).
pattern.notes: 150 questions in 120 minutes; no section-wise time limits stated. All five sections count toward the score. Score report: five sectional scores on a 0-100 scale and a Composite Score on a 200-800 scale (equal weight to all five sections), each with a percentile; raw scores normalized across sessions since Feb 2021.

registrationFee.category: Upgrade to an additional test mode (after registration)
Each additional Management Institute score choice (incl. 18% GST)

resultAndCounselling: Score cards are downloaded from the applicant dashboard on https://mat.aima.in/ (December 2026 results by the first week of January 2027). Scores are released to both candidates and the Management Institutes (MIs) chosen during registration (5 MIs; 7 if two test modes are taken; more at Rs 118 each). Candidates taking both PBT and CBT can use their best score. There is no central counselling: each participating institute (AICTE-approved, DEC-approved, university-affiliated colleges or university departments) applies its own admission criteria. AIMA states MAT scores are accepted by 600+ B-Schools.
